name: TFM-4AS-1

lead: TFM-4AS-1 is a lab-stage steroidal SARM first described in 2009. In rats it increased muscle and bone while having smaller effects on reproductive organs and oil-producing skin glands than a related full agonist.
No human study of it was found.

paras: It partially activates the androgen receptor and blocks the receptor's internal N/C-terminal interaction, so it switches on only some androgen-responsive genes.
Human safety is unknown. It is not approved for any use.

lead: TFM-4AS-1 is an experimental steroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) described in a 2009 paper in the Journal of Biological Chemistry. It belongs to the 4-aza-steroid class and was characterized as a potent androgen receptor ligand that only partially activates the receptor.[1]

In that study, ovariectomized rats given TFM-4AS-1 gained bone and muscle mass while showing reduced effects on reproductive organs and sebaceous glands, and the compound did not promote prostate growth.[1] The sources reviewed contain no human studies of TFM-4AS-1, and it has no approved use.

paras: The authors reported that TFM-4AS-1 binds the androgen receptor with an IC50 of 38 nM, activates an androgen-dependent promoter to about 55 percent of the maximal response, and antagonizes the interaction between the receptor's N- and C-terminal regions needed for full activation.[1] Gene-expression analysis in a breast cancer cell line showed it induced some androgen-responsive genes as strongly as dihydrotestosterone and others weakly or not at all, which the authors proposed as a basis for tissue selectivity.[1] They compared it with a closely related full agonist, Cl-4AS-1, and with an unrelated compound, FTBU-1, which showed similar partial-agonist behavior.[1]

No studies found. In preclinical work, ovariectomized rats treated with TFM-4AS-1 accrued bone and muscle with reduced effects on reproductive tissues and sebaceous glands compared with the full agonist.[1]

TFM-4AS-1 is among the chemical classes included in some analytical reviews and mixture-modelling studies of androgen receptor ligands, and SARMs in general are monitored in anti-doping testing.[2][3] The sources reviewed do not document use of TFM-4AS-1 in looksmaxxing communities.

timeline.event: TFM-4AS-1 described as a tissue-selective SARM in rats.[1]
